title: Applied AI engineering: build and evaluate LLM systems
goal: Learn to build products on top of language models: prompting and structured output, retrieval, tool use and agents, and above all how to evaluate and secure them, because the data shows verification is the scarce skill.

steps.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
steps.note: Transformers, tokenization, fine-tuning and the ecosystem, hands-on.

steps.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero (Andrej Karpathy)
steps.note: Build a small language model from scratch to understand what the APIs hide.

steps.title: AI Engineering (Chip Huyen)
steps.note: Evaluation, RAG, agents and production concerns; the most practical overview of the discipline.

steps.title: Building effective agents (Anthropic)
steps.note: Patterns for workflows and agents, and when simpler solutions are better.

steps.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications
steps.note: Prompt injection, data leakage and other risks you must design against.

steps.title: A retrieval-augmented app with an evaluation harness
steps.brief: Build a question-answering app over a document set you choose. Write at least 50 test questions with expected answers, measure retrieval and answer quality separately, change one thing at a time (chunking, embeddings, prompts) and record the effect.
steps.deliverable: A repository with the app, the evaluation set, a script that prints scores and a README table showing which changes helped.

steps.title: A tool-using agent with guardrails
steps.brief: Build an agent that calls two or three real tools, with input validation, a step limit, timeouts, retries with backoff and logging of every tool call. Test it against adversarial inputs from the OWASP list.
steps.deliverable: A repository with the agent, a test suite of failure and attack cases, and a short write-up of what broke and how you fixed it.

steps.title: LLM system design and ML system design lessons
steps.note: SD module 26 (feature stores, serving, A/B testing) and LLM-specific design are not written on this site yet. Use the books above and design the two projects as if for production: latency, cost, caching, queueing and failure modes.

exit: You can explain how retrieval, prompting and evaluation each affect answer quality, with measurements from your own project.
Your evaluation harness catches a regression you introduced on purpose.
You can describe three ways your agent can fail or be attacked and the mitigation for each.
You use AI tools daily for implementation but can say what you verified and how.
